title: Google gains US smartphone market ground as Samsung and Motorola slip
summary: This comes despite an year-over-over decline.
body: TL;DR Google’s Pixel 11 series helped double its US smartphone shipment market share from 3% in Q2 2026 to 6% in Q3 2026. Despite the quarterly growth, Google’s market share remains below the 7% it held in Q3 2025, while Samsung and Motorola also lost ground quarter-over-quarter. Apple dominated the US market with a 57% shipment share, even as overall smartphone shipments declined 9% year-over-year. The Pixel 11 series has proven to be a much-needed boost for Google’s US smartphone market share, essentially doubling the company’s shipments from 3% in Q2 2026 to 6% in Q3 2026. That win, however, appears to have come at the expense of competitors like Samsung and Motorola , with Google still struggling to match its performance from the same period last year. The new information comes via Counterpoint Research’s latest data , which highlights how the US smartphone market performed in Q3 2026. For reference, the Pixel 11 series came out in August, so it makes sense that Google experienced a meaningful boost, going from 3% shipment market share to 6% quarter-over-quarter.

title: Signal is blocking screenshots to prevent Gemini and Siri AI from scanning your chats
summary: Signal wants AI assistants to stay out of your private conversations.
body: TL;DR Signal is introducing protections to prevent Gemini and Siri AI from scanning private conversations on Android and iOS 27. The protections also block users from taking screenshots inside Signal, but they can be disabled. Signal is calling on Google, Apple, and Microsoft to give app developers better tools to restrict AI access without compromising app functionality. AI assistants are increasingly doing things on our phones that would previously require us to open an app ourselves. Gemini can already order food and book rides using third-party Android apps , and just yesterday, Google started rolling out similar computer-use capabilities on Macs . Meanwhile, Apple’s Siri AI can understand what’s on your iPhone’s screen. But what happens when the app an AI assistant tries to read contains information that was never meant to leave it? That’s a question Signal is tackling head-on. The encrypted messaging service announced today that it is introducing protections against AI assistants capturing its content on Android and iOS 27.

title: Google brings computer use to Mac, letting Gemini handle chores without hijacking your screen
summary: Let Gemini do the clicking while you do the working.
body: TL;DR Google is rolling out computer use to the Gemini app for Mac, allowing it to operate desktop apps and websites on your behalf. Gemini works in an isolated background window, leaving your screen and cursor free while you monitor its progress in real time. The feature requires an Apple Silicon Mac and a Google AI Plus, Pro, or Ultra subscription, and is initially available in the US. When Google brought Gemini Spark to the Mac earlier this year, it gave its AI assistant access to local files, allowing it to handle chores like organizing folders and turning documents into spreadsheets. But working with files on your computer and actually operating the apps installed on it are two different things. Google’s latest Gemini update bridges that gap. Just two days after making Gemini Tasks available for free and adding the ability to call businesses, make purchases, and accept requests via text and email, Google is rolling out computer use to the Gemini app for Mac . The feature, which we first learned was in testing in September , lets Gemini click buttons, type, navigate menus, and fill out forms across desktop apps and websites on your behalf.

title: Fitbit Edge owners are complaining about the lack of hourly movement reminders
summary: Fitbit Edge tracks your hourly steps, but it won't remind you to take them.
body: TL;DR Fitbit Edge owners report that the tracker lacks hourly reminders to move. The tracker still monitors hourly activity but doesn’t vibrate to remind users to reach their 250-step goal. Reminders to move have been available on Fitbit devices since 2016, helping users stay active throughout the day. One of the simplest ways Fitbit has helped people stay active over the years is by encouraging them to get out of their chairs. As far back as the original Fitbit Alta in 2016, Fitbit offered reminders to move. Rather than letting you cram all your daily steps into an evening walk, the feature encouraged you to spread your activity throughout the day. However, those upgrading to the new Google Fitbit Edge are discovering that their wrists have gone unusually quiet. Reports on Reddit , Facebook ( 2 ), and the Google Health Community reveal that the Fitbit Edge lacks an option to enable hourly reminders to move. While the tracker still records hourly activity, it apparently doesn’t vibrate to remind you when you’re falling short of your 250-step hourly goal.
